TESTIMONY OF THE DEPARTMENT OF INLAND FISHERIES AND WILDLIFE
BEFORE THE JOINT STANDING COMMITTEE ON INLAND FISHERIES AND WILDLIFE
In Opposition to L.D. 1448
"An Act to Provide Winter Access to the Bog Lake Public Boat Launch in
Northfield"
Presented by Senator MOORE of Washington. (BY REQUEST)
Cosponsored by Representative TUELL of East Machias.
DATE OF HEARING: Monday, April 14, 2025
Good afternoon, Senator Baldacci, Representative Roberts and members of the Inland Fisheries and Wildlife Committee. I am Diano Circo the Chief Planner at the Department of Inland Fisheries and
Wildlife (IFW), speaking on behalf of the Department in opposition to L.D. 1448 - An Act to Provide Winter Access to the Bog Lake Public Boat Launch in Northfield.
This bill requires the Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife to ensure the gate to the Bog Lake public boat launch in the Town of Northfield is open from January ls` to March 15"` each year.
The Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife owns and manages 182 water access sites across the state. These facilities provide critical public access to Maine's publicly held waters during all seasons. The Bog Lake property was purchased in 2001 and developed in 2013 after a lengthy and extensive permitting process. The Maine Department of Environmental Protection Stormwater Permit for the facility required substantial design and construction detail that resulted in a considerable stormwater
management system that parallels the over % mile long gravel access road to the launch.
To prevent damage to the access road and stormwater infrastructure, the Department closes the Bog Lake gate prior to the first significant snowfall each winter and reopens it in the spring when staff have determined the road is dry and firm enough for larger vehicles. In the winter, parking is provided next to
the gate and anglers can access the site by foot, ATV or snowmobile. This is consistent with how the
Department manages other water access facilities with significant stormwater infrastructure of this type
and many of our Wildlife Management Area road systems.
As an example of the importance of the gate, in the winter of 2021, the gate at the Bog Lake facility was opened without authorization. This resulted in damage to the road that required $5,000 in repairs, and
ongoing challenges for maintenance of the stormwater system that has increased yearly maintenance costs going forward.
For these reasons we are opposed to this bill and would ask the Committee to carefully consider these
concerns.
I would be glad to answer any questions at this time or during the work session.

To: IF&W Committee From Steven Pineo

My name is Steven Pineo. I am a camp owner at Bog Lake in Northfield, Maine.

Today I am writing to testify for approval of LD 1448, an act to Provide Winter Access to the Bog Lake Public Launch in Northfield, Maine. It is with great disappointment that we have to ask IF & W to provide fair and equitable access to the public landing at Bog Lake. The issue we have is the gate to the landing being closed and locked restricting access during the Winter months. The gate is closed and locked at some point around December 1st and does not get opened back up until after "Mud Season" sometime around April 1st. The concerned camp owners around the lake cannot understand why this gate cannot be opened during the winter months once the road is frozen.
Bog Lake is a very popular lake for ice fishing and Winter activities. In fact, the camp owners around the lake now put on an ice fishing derby every winter, when ice conditions allow, to benefit different schools around the county. It is a very popular event! This year we had 3 local grade schools attend and send buses to get the kids to the lake. The issue is getting buses close enough to the lake to make it easy for kids and parents to attend. Use of the "Public" landing would fix this issue.
The last two winters we have contacted Inland Fisheries and Wildlife to ask if we could get the gate opened for the Winter. We also have asked if we could simply get it opened for just our events. The local office has tried to help make this happen for us but the answer from Augusta has been "absolutely not"!
When this landing was proposed to the town in 2016 it was presented to the concerned citizens as being needed for fair and equitable access to the lake. This statement comes directly from the department's fish stocking program policy. The first few Winters the gate was open. It has only been the last two winters that the department has decided to restrict access and has gone directly against their own policy. They need to be forced to hold up to their end of the agreement! There are landings all over our state that are open for the winter months. Why is Bog Lake any different?

Unfortunately, common sense and a simple phone calls have not worked to fix this issue. Today, I am requesting you require the department to follow their own policy and allow fair and equitable access to the Bog Lake Landing from January 1st ~ March 15th

Steven M. Pineo, Concerned citizen of Bog Lake
